followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: model capability and the nature of the query.

On capability, Willet-235B is consistently stronger than Dunlin-235B across the board — higher public benchmarks (Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 82.7, MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, GPQA 64.1 vs 55.6) and higher internal routing evals on every dimension, including the ones most relevant here like Support Dialogue and Summarization. When a query is benign and could go to either model, the higher-capability model is the sensible default.

On the query itself: it's a neutral, practical request for cross-cultural business advice. There's nothing harm-adjacent, hostile, or ethically fraught about it. That matters because the models' main differentiator beyond raw capability is their task-preference profiles — Dunlin has a strong aversion to distasteful or harmful content, and Willet is comparatively flat on that dimension. But since this query triggers neither model's aversion, those preference differences don't come into play, and the decision falls back to capability.

So the reasoning was: benign content means no preference-based reason to steer toward Dunlin, and capability favors Willet — therefore Willet.
